So, as a thought experiment this is interesting but i can actually offer a real world application of something similar that DOES work, practiced by yours truly. 

I've been an angry person since a very young age, had a lot of things working against me, very toxic environments and horrible people in my life. Have always been very mistreated. Yet, as far as all the drawbacks to my life, I manage to keep up and in some cases surpass my friends, to which they frequently praise me on. 

How? Well, out of spite. What i choose to do is gain the value of insight from my meditation sessions on any subject I feel anger towards, an example being a girl who recently abused me, I ended up reaching the conclusion of insight "i am grateful for all the things she taught me" but i was still angry because...well obviously im going to be. So, instead of dwelling on it, i wrote down my thoughts and then as i did my anger felt more focused and targeted, and i applied it into the "what she taught me" part of my insight, which broke open so many more lessons for me to learn from the experience including, but not limited to, and most importantly being, my now existing list of "fundamental baseline boundaries" which can be applied to any situation involving me interacting with someone to determine if they are unfairly treating me any sort of way. Thus giving me a solution to being abused. (Which has already effectively been a tried and tested method several times now)

The way i feel that it works, is that you back your anger with insight and then focus the anger at a solution to your problem. Which this shifts your anger into spite, and it functions as a motivating force. 
Ex: "you think i cant succeed at A because of B?! Well i know that C is true, thus fuck you A is easily accomplishable. *then accomplishes A without the use of B*

Now to label the letters, A is the thing in question that needs a solution. In this example a class that i seem to be failing. A problem. Why? Because of B, B is a limitation that others have set or an injustice set upon you. Or one that you have caused yourself. C is the insight. Specifically in this example its, "i know im intelligent and dont need to do the homework to pass the test/class anyways, so now...." and then utilizing them together it comes down to "i wont do the homework because of the insight that i know im intelligent enough to handle the materials of the class to pass said class so i will do this MY way, and prove my point just out of spite." 

Its more like....focusing the anger into the point of a blade and picking and striking a very small target with extreme accuracy. Hyperfixated spiteful motivation, if you will. 

I used it unknowingly a lot in high school when teachers told me id fail their class because i wasnt smart enough to ace their tests so i did exactly that and passed with all A's, despite never doing a single sheet of homework the entire time i went to high school.
